featured_reviews.name: Suraaj Dubey
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited the hospital for blood donation with a genuine intention to help others. During the screening, I was told that my hemoglobin level was low. However, after further tests, everything came out normal and there was no health issue found.

I feel the staff handling the blood donation process need better training and proper knowledge. Hiring inexperienced staff without enough medical understanding can create unnecessary fear and confusion for donors. Because of this, people who come forward for a good cause may feel discouraged from donating blood again.

I hope the hospital management improves staff training and ensures accurate guidance is given to donors in the future.

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Maurya
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointed with the Treatment Approach

I recently had a deeply disappointing experience at this hospital concerning my mother's health. She was admitted for one day due to a gastric issue. All her reports came back normal, and she was feeling better the next day. Despite this, the doctor insisted on keeping her admitted for an additional three days—without providing a clear medical justification.

When we asked for an explanation, we were told vaguely that she needed antibiotics and "the treatment wasn't complete." It felt more like an excuse to prolong the stay and increase the charges, rather than a decision based on genuine medical necessity.

What’s worse, when I questioned this, the doctor reacted defensively, citing her MBBS degree etc. She then asked me and my father to leave the consultation room, which was both rude and unprofessional.

This experience has left us with serious concerns about the hospital's intentions and patient care ethics. I urge others to seek a second opinion and prioritize preventive healthcare—eat well, stay active, and consult transparent medical professionals who truly have the patient’s best interest at heart.

HbA1c Test: Purpose, Procedure, Normal Range & Results
May 26, 2026 - By Lupin Diagnostics
India has over 10.1 crore people living with diabetes. A daily finger-prick reading captures just one moment. The HbA1c test normal range tells a fuller story. This simple blood test reveals your average blood sugar over three months. Here is everything you need to know about it.
What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
It does not swing based on a recent meal or exercise session.

The test typically measures ALT (SGPT), AST (SGOT), bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase, and albumin levels. Together, these markers reveal the type and location of liver damage. Unlike a single blood sugar reading, an LFT panel paints a broader picture of your liver's overall health.

They messaged me saying that pls come as donate as there is a tremendous shortage. I reached there and was shooed away and told, "Come tomorrow". Not at all professional.

featured_reviews.name: Vikrant Mahulkar
featured_reviews.review_text: Disappointing experience! Donated blood at NMMC camp, but Navjivan Blood Bank refused to help when I needed it for my dad's surgery. Forced to buy blood instead! Unacceptable! Staff seemed unconcerned. Expected more from a reputable blood bank. 1/5 stars. Would not recommend.

featured_reviews.name: Vinaykumar G
featured_reviews.review_text: They charge ₹500 per bag as processing charges which is again not refundable. With me, they showed up one day before the surgery and asked me to pay Rs. 1500 as blood reserve charges which will be refunded if the blood is not used. As we did not use aby blood during surgery we asked them to refund. But they now say it's not refundable as they used it as processing charges. They also do not issue any receipt for payment made. They just work on threats and make the relatives scared that  you better pay me else blood will not be available to you when you require. Totally disgusting service.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavana Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
They are charging ₹500 per bag as deposit just to block the bag. But deposit is never refunded. They say they charge it as testing charges. The blood was not used also during operation. We had booked 3 bags. ₹1500.
I wonder if our booked bag was not used then why to take money. In anyway they are going to use it for someone else.
Whenever we donate blood (free of cost) we assume that it would be helpful to the needy but what we understood from the incident that it's not freely given to the needy.
